lane: معذ معذ 1 , [aor. ﹷ, inf. n. مَعَرٌ,] said of a man, (S,) and of the head, and of the tail, (TA,) His or its hair fell off; (S, TA;) as also ↓تمعّر, said of the head: (TA:) and the former said of the head, its hair became little, or scanty. (TA:) and مَعِرَتْ, said of the forelock, (النَّاصِيَة, K,) or of that of a horse, (TA,) it lost all its hair: (K:) and مَعِرَ, said of a solid hoof, it lost the hair that hung down upon it from the fore part of the pastern. (TA.) === مَعِرَ, (A, K,) aor. ﹷ, (K,) inf. n. مَعَرٌ, (S, TA,) said of hair, (S, A, K,) and of plumage, and the like, (K,) It fell off; (S, A;) as also ↓تمعّر, said of hair: (S, A:) or it became little, or scanty; as also ↓أَمْعَرَ: (K:) and, said of a finger-nail, or toe-nail, ‡ it came out, or fell out, (A, K,) in consequence of something befalling it, or hurting it. (K.) See مَعَرَّةٌ in art. عر. === [Hence,] مَعِرَ, (TA,) or مَعِرَ مِنْ مَالِهِ, (A,) ‡ He became poor; (A, TA;) as also ↓أَمْعَرَ, (S, A,) inf. n. إِمْعَارٌ; (TA;) or the latter, he became poor, and his travelling-provisions failed or became exhausted; as also ↓معّر, inf. n. تَمْعِيرٌ. (K.) === [Hence also,] ↓أَمْعَرَتِالأَرْضُ ‡ The land became destitute of herbage: or its herbage became little, or scanty: (K:) contr. of أَمْرَعَت. (IKtt.)
